parakeet: Supremacy always promises protection, but it delivers fracture instead. And it doesn't just harm the people it dominates, it quietly reshapes the people who carry it. Christian supremacy often demands silence when harm is visible, justification when violence is done for good, and rationalization when policies or practices hurt real people in real time. Over time, something breaks. People learn how to explain away what they feel instead of listening to it. That disconnect doesn't disappear, it just hardens. Faith becomes exhausting, not because belief is heavy, but because conscience is constantly overridden. You can't dominate people that you fully see. So others become categories instead of neighbors, threats instead of humans, and symbols instead of stories. And I caution the secular, atheist, and humanist community to stop falling for the same fucking trap. Stop dehumanizing other people. Period. If there is any good reason to dehumanize another person, then there is always an acceptable reason to dehumanize another person. Even when no physical violence occurs, humanity erodes. And here's the quiet damage. Once you train yourself not to see the humanity in them, your capacity to see it in anyone diminishes, including yourself. Empathy threatens supremacy because empathy destabilizes hierarchy. So people are trained, often unconsciously, to look away, minimize harm, distrust emotional responses, and even prioritize doctrine over experience. This suppression doesn't make people stronger, it makes them numb. And numbness doesn't stop at the boundary of belief. It leaks into relationships, into parenting, into community, and even into self-understanding. Supremacy eventually consumes its own believers. It isolates them, hardens them, exhausts them. No one can live well while holding the world at arm's length.
